_metadata.description: Direct jobs per $1M of commercial casino gaming revenue (2023 dollars) as a function of the gaming tax rate. Replaces the state gambling jobs coefficient for the gaming stream of commercial stand-alone casinos and casino hotels.
_metadata.method: Regression of log(observed jobs per $1M of gaming revenue) on the state's effective gaming tax rate, standard errors clustered by state. Cells: 2022 Economic Census stand-alone casinos (employees / receipts) and casino hotels (employees minus modeled non-gaming jobs, per dollar of gaming receipts from the Census product lines), states with commercial casinos, cells with at least 50 employees, receipts in 2023 dollars. jobs per $1M = level x exp(-slope x rate).
_metadata.rationale: Across these cells the state gambling jobs coefficient (QCEW jobs in sector 713 / StateIO output, with the national gambling ratio) has no correlation with observed jobs per revenue dollar (r = -0.08), and observed jobs per revenue dollar fall with the gaming tax carried in revenue. In leave-one-state-out prediction the national rate has a lower error than the state coefficient, and than the state coefficient multiplied by a tax factor.
_metadata.rate: The effective rate the analysis applies to gaming revenue: the computed statutory or custom rate when gaming revenue is entered, otherwise the state's blended effective rate.
_metadata.consequences: Changes direct jobs and direct estimated FTEs of the gaming stream only. Compensation, value added, supplier and induced effects do not change. User-entered jobs replace the value.
_metadata.scope: Commercial stand-alone casinos (713210) and casino hotels (721120): the gaming department, or all revenue when only total revenue is entered. Not applied to slot parlors and bingo halls (the national rate does not lower their error), bars with slots, tribal properties (outside the sample) or online operators; these keep the state coefficient.
_metadata.limits: 21 cells in 15 states. For the casino-hotel cells alone the slope is not significant (p = 0.18) and the rate is not better than a national constant. The casino-hotel cells depend on the model's lodging, food and other coefficients. The rate is linear in revenue: Nevada Gaming Abstract data (fiscal year 2025) show about half the jobs per revenue dollar at the largest casinos compared with small casinos.
_metadata.ranges: 90% predictive ranges of true / predicted direct jobs. Gaming department and stand-alone casinos: leave-one-state-out errors. Casino hotels entered as total revenue: the rate applied to all receipts of 15 casino-hotel cells; the range includes the resulting bias (non-gaming departments have more jobs per dollar).
_metadata.source: Replication repository kphilander/casino-io-validation, script 19c, analysis_output/direct_jobs_rate_fit.csv, direct_jobs_rate_loso.csv and direct_jobs_rate_ranges.csv; private until publication. Data: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Economic Census, EC2271BASIC, EC2272BASIC and product lines of NAICS 721120.
